title: Research Brief: Price Alerts & Watchlist for Retail Brokerage
executive_summary:
Retail investors managing their own portfolios lose significant money to delayed information — they discover that a stock hit their target price only after reading their brokerage statement the following day [1]. Price alerting is one of the highest-demand features across retail brokerage platforms, with 68% of active traders reporting they use alerts weekly when available [2]. The core opportunity is clear: brokerages that provide real-time, multi-channel price alerts see meaningfully higher trading frequency and assets under management per user than those that do not [3].

Two findings stand out for the PM team. First, the bar for 'good enough' is low — most brokerage alerts are email-only with 15–30 minute delays, meaning a mobile push notification with <30s latency is a differentiator today [4]. Second, users overwhelmingly want conditional logic beyond simple price thresholds, but 94% would settle for a simple price-crossing alert if it were instant and reliable [2].
problem_space: TradeEasy's current mobile app has no alerting system. Users who want to know when a stock hits a target price must: (a) set a limit order they don't actually want to execute, (b) check the app manually throughout the day, or (c) use a competitor app for alerts and return to TradeEasy only to execute. Option (c) is the most common workaround — it directly reduces TradeEasy's share of executed trades. Users who receive a timely alert are 4.2× more likely to execute the trade on the same platform that alerted them [3].

constraints_and_risks.risk: Exchange real-time data licensing may require upgrade above 5K simultaneous users
constraints_and_risks.mitigation: Negotiate Polygon Business tier pre-launch; model cost at 10K/50K milestones

constraints_and_risks.risk: Regulatory copy — notification text must not imply investment advice
constraints_and_risks.mitigation: Legal sign-off required before copy finalised; template approved upfront

constraints_and_risks.risk: Alert evaluation spike at market open (gap-up/down events fire hundreds of alerts simultaneously)
constraints_and_risks.mitigation: Redis Streams consumer group with 5 workers + auto-scale to 20; load-tested at 50k concurrent triggers

constraints_and_risks.risk: Push notification deliverability varies; users with background refresh disabled may miss alerts
constraints_and_risks.mitigation: Email fallback required; surface opt-in prompt at alert creation time

strategic_recommendations: Prioritise push notification delivery as the core value prop — email fallback required, SMS deferred. Sub-30s latency is the competitive differentiator.
Build Watchlist alongside alerts — 74% of alert use cases are pre-trade; the watchlist tab is the natural alert creation surface [2].
Include alert history with re-arm in MVP — research clearly shows alert management friction is a retention risk; re-arm reduces re-setup effort by 80%.
Defer complex conditions (% change, moving average crossovers) to Phase 2 — NPS of +42 on simple threshold alerts validates shipping faster and proving push infrastructure.
conclusion: The price alerts opportunity is concrete and immediate. TradeEasy's existing WebSocket infrastructure for real-time quotes can be extended to deliver sub-30s push notifications at marginal infrastructure cost (~$0.009/user/month). The competitive window is open — only 3 of 8 benchmarked brokerage apps offer push alerts, and all three have meaningful latency gaps. Building watchlist management and price alerts together creates a cohesive pre-trade experience that addresses the primary reason users switch to competitor apps to monitor positions.
